Atomoxetin (ATC code N06BA09) is a non-stimulant norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor used in the treatment of ADHD. Within the context of the Danish national ADHD database quality monitoring, it is tracked as one of the core pharmacological treatments for the condition.

In the 2023 ADHD database report, Atomoxetin was identified as one of six specific ADHD medications included in the calculation of [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]], which measures pharmacological treatment coverage among ADHD patients in standard care pathways [^src1]. This indicator highlights regional variations in medical treatment practices across Denmark [^src1]. The medication's inclusion in [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] was reiterated in the 2024 national ADHD report, which evaluated quantitative results for the measurement period spanning April 1, 2024, to March 31, 2025 [^src2]. The 2024 report noted that while there are systemic challenges in non-pharmacological interventions like psychoeducation, pharmacological treatment remains a relative strength in the Danish ADHD effort, with specific regional variations [^src2].

Furthermore, as the ADHD database expanded its scope to include adults—previously focusing only on children and adolescents—Atomoxetin was also incorporated into the newly introduced [[indikator-11|Indikator 11]] [^src3]. This indicator, detailed in the 2024 report, tracks pharmacological treatment among adult ADHD patients, utilizing data from the National Patient Registry (LPR) and medicine statistics [^src3]. Atomoxetin is listed alongside other medications such as dexamphetamine, methylphenidate, modafinil, lisdexamphetamine, and guanfacine in this adult treatment metric [^src3].
